findings.claim: SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is dead work on the webhook and cron cache-refresh hot path. Its new repository method (packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405) is dead too. With empty data under Prisma 5.4.2 it likely does not bump @updatedAt at all, so the comment above it is misleading. Even if it did bump the column, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, because the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt.
findings.evidence: Two seats grep-verified that nothing consumes it: ponytail found that updateManyByCredentialId has only the definition and this one caller, and superpowers found no reader of .updatedAt or googleChannelId in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts. The no-op claim under Prisma 5.4.2 (yarn.lock:38872) is reasoned by open-code-review and superpowers and was not checked against a DB. mattpocock also flags the bump as unverified. The call runs through webhook.ts:46 to fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Fix by removing the call and the unused repository method. Red check: a test that spies on SelectedCalendarRepository during fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache and asserts no SelectedCalendar write. It fails on the pinned code. The secondary claim that empty-data updateMany leaves updatedAt unchanged stays reasoned and unverified (it needs a live DB), and it becomes moot once the call is removed.

verifier.reason: The call at CalendarService.ts:1024 and its helper at selectedCalendar.ts:400-405 do work nobody uses. The patch's UI timestamp comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:31-35 → CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69-92), and no code reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (schema.prisma:860), even though user.ts:899 now selects it. I did not run this against Prisma, but with empty data Prisma most likely skips the @updatedAt bump, so the comment at line 1023 is probably misleading too.

findings.claim: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS-only. On GNU sed (Linux) the .env update fails, and the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated.
findings.evidence: open-code-review, ponytail and superpowers each reproduced it independently. `printf 'GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=old\n' > t.env; sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=new|' t.env` gives `sed: can't read s|...: No such file or directory`, exit 2, and the file is unchanged. superpowers cites line 56 and the other seats cite 68. This is the same claim.
findings.reason: Reproduced, with a ready red command. Severities were split (two Important, two Minor). Normalised to Important because the failure is silent and reports false success. Either a portable in-place edit or dropping the script from the PR (see the appendix scope note) closes it.

verifier.reason: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 runs `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`. GNU sed takes the separate `''` as an empty script and the `s|...|` expression as a filename, so it fails with 'can't read' and leaves .env unchanged. Line 73 still prints '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL' because it never checks the sed exit status.

findings.claim: ENV_FILE="../.env" depends on the directory the script is run from.
findings.evidence: All four seats note the relative path. The script only works when run from a directory whose parent holds .env.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Resolve the path relative to the script's own location, or drop the script from the PR.

verifier.reason: At scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5, ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved against the directory the script is run from, not the script's own location, and nothing in the repo calls the script from a fixed directory. If it is run from the repo root, lines 62-70 create or edit a .env outside the repo instead of the project's .env.

findings.claim: A failed ownership check throws a plain Error, so the client gets a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.
findings.evidence: The sibling setDestinationCalendar.handler.ts imports TRPCError (line 7) and throws it with specific codes (lines 77 and 97).
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Use new TRPCError({ code: 'NOT_FOUND' }), which matches the local convention.

verifier.reason: deleteCache.handler.ts:25 throws a plain `new Error(...)`. tRPC turns any non-TRPCError into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, and nothing here maps it to another code: errorFormatter.ts:25-38 only special-cases ZodError, and the authedProcedure middleware does not catch it.

findings.claim: The deleteCache input schema is an inline z.object. It is not a deleteCache.schema.ts file, and it is not added to the CalendarsRouterHandlerCache type the way sibling procedures are.
findings.evidence: Sibling procedures use connectedCalendars.schema.ts and setDestinationCalendar.schema.ts (ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema, ZSetDestinationCalendarInputSchema) and are listed in lines 1-11 of the same file.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Follow the router convention.

verifier.reason: At _router.tsx:29 the patch passes an inline `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })` instead of importing it from a deleteCache.schema.ts file, and the CalendarsRouterHandlerCache type (lines 8-11) lists only connectedCalendars and setDestinationCalendar. That type isn't used anywhere in this file, so leaving deleteCache out of it has no effect at runtime.

findings.claim: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select in findUnlockedUserForSession, and the UserWithCalendars type is widened to match (packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28). Nothing reads either field, yet every session lookup fetches them, and the fields are required in the type.
findings.evidence: Greps by mattpocock, ponytail and superpowers find the fields only in type lines. This breaches the .cursor/rules/review.mdc rule 'Only select data you need'. superpowers notes that the v1 caller (apps/api/v1/pages/api/connected-calendars/_get.ts) and the v2 caller (calendars.service.ts) currently fit the widened type.
findings.reason: Four seats agree, and it breaches a documented standard. Revert both hunks.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to the `selectedCalendars` select at packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900 and as required fields in `UserWithCalendars` (packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28), but no code path reads them: `getConnectedCalendars` takes only `{ externalId }[]` (packages/lib/CalendarManager.ts:53), and the new cache UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt`, which comes from the `CalendarCache` table, not `SelectedCalendar`.

findings.claim: The 'Last updated' timestamp uses a hard-coded new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...). It ignores the user's locale and profile timezone, while the label next to it goes through t().
findings.evidence: The literal 'en-US' locale is in the source. review.mdc says 'Always use t() for text localization in frontend code'. superpowers cites lines 139-142, likely a different numbering basis, for the same call.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Use the locale from useLocale.

verifier.reason: In the new file packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx (lines 89-92, which are patch lines 139-142), the timestamp is built with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` and no `timeZone` option, so it ignores the user's locale and profile timezone (it falls back to the browser's zone), while the surrounding label goes through `t("cache_last_updated")`, even though `useLocale()` is already available on line 37.

findings.claim: The handler builds new CalendarCacheRepository() directly. That bypasses the calendar-cache feature-flag gate and the CalendarCache factory (calendar-cache.ts:24-28). Cache status and 'Delete cached data' therefore appear even when caching is off, and the new CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds and the interface addition (calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts:30-32, calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:26-30) are unreachable.
findings.evidence: calendar-cache.ts:27-28 returns the mock when the flag is off, and this call path never goes through it.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Route through the factory or flag check, or drop the unreachable interface and mock edits.

verifier.reason: The handler does build `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28), so the flag check is skipped. But the claimed UI effect does not happen: toggling 'calendar-cache' off deletes every CalendarCache row (toggleFeatureFlag.handler.ts:32-34), and while the flag is off, writes go to the mock (calendar-cache.ts:27-28), so the query returns nothing, `cacheUpdatedAt` stays null and the dropdown hides cache status and 'Delete cached data' (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx `hasCache`); the unused mock method is only a nit.

findings.claim: An undocumented behaviour change: in the error/Alert branch, 'Remove app' used to be hidden only for delegation credentials. It is now also hidden when disableConnectionModification is set, so users in that view can no longer remove a broken credential.
findings.evidence: The removed lines checked only !connectedCalendar.delegationCredentialId. The new CredentialActionsDropdown also gates on !disableConnectionModification, which is set whenever the scope is disabled (line 168). No commit mentions the change.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Restore the previous gating on the error branch unless the change is intended. With no spec, intent cannot be confirmed. Red check: render the error branch with disableConnectionModification=true and expect 'Remove app'.

verifier.reason: In the error/Alert branch, the old code showed Remove app whenever there was no delegationCredentialId. It now renders CredentialActionsDropdown (SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:123-131), which hides Remove app when disableConnectionModification is true (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68). The evidence overstates one point: line 182 passes the raw disableConnectionModification prop, not shouldDisableConnectionModification, so a disabled scope (isDisabled) alone does not hide the option.

findings.claim: dev:cron switches from ts-node (still declared at line 196) to npx tsx. tsx is not declared and not in yarn.lock, so npx downloads it from the registry at run time. The change is also unrelated to the feature.
findings.evidence: open-code-review and superpowers grepped the package.json files and yarn.lock and found no tsx dependency.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Revert, or move to a separate PR.

verifier.reason: The patch changes apps/web/package.json:11 from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, while `ts-node` is still declared at apps/web/package.json:196. No package.json or yarn.lock entry declares tsx, so npx fetches an unpinned copy at run time, and this has nothing to do with the cache-status feature in the rest of the patch.
